extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy of biology / metaphysics (readers of Bergson's Creative Evolution)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and methodological prescriptions for assessing accounts of life and evolution, especially the tension between mechanism and finalism and how to test them (e.g., via comparative anatomy, adaptation arguments, and the role of intuition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe importance (vague intuition)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the fringe exists, however delicate and indistinct, it should have more importance for philosophy than the bright nucleus it surrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical method should attend not only to the clear, intellectual 'nucleus' but to the surrounding vague intuitions (the 'fringe'); the fringe indicates that intellect is a contraction of a more extensive power and supplies hints necessary to expand intellectual forms of thought. Do not ignore or dismiss indistinct intuition when attempting to grasp life as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incommensurability of free acts
rubrics_metrics.description: A conduct that is truly our own... could not have been foreseen, even though its antecedents explain it when once it has been accomplished... The free act is incommensurable with the idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating human action, distinguish genuine free action (which cannot be predicted from antecedents and is not mere caprice) from mechanical oscillation among ready-made alternatives. 'Rationality' of free acts must be defined by their incommensurability with intellectual ideas; do not reduce freedom to predictability or mere imitation of intellect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid forcing new objects into ready-made concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Our reason... imagines itself possessed of all the essential elements of the knowledge of truth... The idea that for a new object we might have to create a new concept... is deeply repugnant to us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments and theories must avoid merely slotting novel phenomena into pre-existing categories. Be prepared to create new concepts and new methods of thinking rather than forcing the real into ready-made intellectual garments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part is not equivalent to whole (representing life)
rubrics_metrics.description: To form an idea of the whole of life cannot consist in combining simple ideas that have been left behind in us by life itself... How could the part be equivalent to the whole?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not infer the character of the entire evolutionary movement from a single evolved terminal or by assembling leftover intellectual fragments. A satisfactory representation of life requires integrating diverse elements from multiple terminal points of evolution, since the evolved is only a result, not the act of evolution itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcend both mechanism and classic finalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Such is the philosophy of life to which we are leading up. It claims to transcend both mechanism and finalism; but... it is nearer the second doctrine than the first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating theories of life, seek a standpoint that moves beyond the limitations of radical mechanism and of classic finalism: recognize complementarity and creative expansion without positing a pre-existing, fully determinate end. Avoid simplistic teleological readings that assume the future is contained as an idea in the present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convergent complex-structure test of mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure mechanism, then, would be refutable, and finality... would be demonstrable in a certain aspect, if it could be proved that life may manufacture the like apparatus, by unlike means, on divergent lines of evolution; and the strength of the proof would be proportional both to the divergency between the lines of evolution thus chosen and to the complexity of the similar structures found in them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cases of similar, highly complex organs arising on clearly divergent evolutionary lines (convergent structures) as a key empirical test: the greater the divergence between lineages and the greater the complexity of the similar structures, the stronger the argument against pure accidental/mechanistic explanation and the stronger the case for a notion of finality or common impulsion. Apply this test concretely (e.g., compare vertebrate and mollusc eyes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation ambiguity — passive vs active
rubrics_metrics.description: Adaptation... is supposed to bring about a precise adjustment of the organism to its circumstances. But adaptation has two senses: passive mechanical adjustment (mold) and active reply (organism builds a machine suited to circumstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about which meaning of 'adaptation' is invoked. Passive 'molding' (pre-existing forms forcing shape) cannot account for creative form-generation; active adaptive 'reply' approaches finality or intelligence. Avoid surreptitiously switching between the two senses when arguing for a mechanistic account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organ-to-organ comparative method
rubrics_metrics.description: The discussion would take an entirely different turn... if we began by comparing together two terms of the same nature, an organ with an organ, instead of an organ with its function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodologically prefer direct comparisons of homologous/analogous organs across independently evolving lineages (organ vs organ) rather than organ-function comparisons. This comparative approach better reveals whether similarity results from common causes, adaptation, or something beyond pure mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of cumulative insensible variation (Darwinian gradualism)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the variations invoked are accidental... how can they ever agree to arise in every part of the organ at the same time... How could the same small variations, incalculable in number, have ever occurred in the same order on two independent lines of evolution, if they were purely accidental?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize claims that tiny, cumulative accidental changes can produce coordinated complex structures across divergent lines: coordination across many parts and preservation by selection when intermediary steps confer no advantage is implausible as a sole explanation for high-complexity convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems with sudden (saltational) variation hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: If the eye of the mollusc and that of the vertebrate have both been raised to their present form by a relatively small number of sudden leaps... there arises another problem... how do all the parts of the visual apparatus, suddenly changed, remain so well co-ordinated that the eye continues to exercise its function?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate saltational/sudden-variation accounts for their ability to produce simultaneously coordinated, complementary changes across all parts of an organ. Even if fewer large jumps make convergence easier to imagine, they still demand an explanation of coordinated complementarity rather than random coincidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation law must explain complementary coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: The law of correlation will be invoked... A collective whole of solidary changes is one thing, a system of complementary changes... is another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appeals are made to correlation (changes in one part affecting others), require that the invoked correlation explain complementary, function-preserving or function-improving coordination, not merely solidarity or linked lesions. Correlation as mere common origin cannot by itself account for the fine-tuned complementarity of organs like the eye.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject container-mold metaphor for adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the adaptation of an organism to the circumstances it has to live in, where is the pre-existing form awaiting its matter? The circumstances are not a mold into which life is inserted... There is no form yet, and life must create a form for itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat environmental conditions as pre-formed molds passively shaping organisms. Explanations that rely on a 'container' forcing shape on passive matter are metaphorical and inadequate for accounting for creative form-generation; insist on mechanisms that allow organisms to 'reply' and build fitting forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony as complementarity from common impetus (not teleological end)
rubrics_metrics.description: Harmony, or rather 'complementarity,' is revealed only in the mass, in tendencies rather than in states... harmony is rather behind us than before. It is due to an identity of impulsion and not to a common aspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret observed complementarity among species or organs as resulting from a shared originating impetus and divergent realizations, not as evidence of a pre-existing, teleological end or universal aspiration. Avoid reading harmony as forward-directed purpose; understand it statistically and historically as complementarity emerging from a common source.
